bugs: app/Console/Commands/PurgeExports.php:82 — $disk->delete() is not wrapped in try/catch. FilesystemAdapter::delete only catches UnableToDeleteFile, so any other Flysystem exception aborts the whole run instead of carrying on. My probe proved it: a row with path '../../etc/x.csv' throws PathTraversalDetected, the purge stops and the remaining expired exports are left untouched. That breaks the 'carry on with the rest' requirement.
If the run throws partway through a chunk, files already deleted in that chunk keep their rows until the next run (they self-heal later, but the run gives no summary).

v.rationale:
All four suites pass: impl-2 20 tests, impl-4 19, impl-3 17, impl-1 15. Every implementation also passed my probes for a real permission-denied directory, 2,500 rows with mixed failures, and the 30-day boundary. A further probe used a row with the path '../../etc/x.csv', and only impl-1 failed it: Flysystem throws PathTraversalDetected, impl-1 has no try/catch around the delete, and the whole run stops, which breaks the 'carry on with the rest' requirement. That puts it last.

impl-2 and impl-4 are nearly the same design: ConfirmableTrait, lazyById over an attribute scope, catching Throwable and calling report(), a cache lock released in finally, INVALID exit code for bad --days. impl-2 ranks first because its tests are more complete: they cover both accepting and declining the confirmation, while impl-4 relies on the prompt's default answer and never tests acceptance. impl-4 has the leaner query (it selects only id and path) and a longer lock TTL. impl-2's 1h TTL is a small risk of overlap on very long runs.

impl-3 is correct and has the most efficient deletes (one bulk DELETE per chunk), but it is less idiomatic: it reinvents the confirmation instead of using ConfirmableTrait, has no model scope, leaves parameters untyped, uses the old signature properties, and builds the query from a closure.
